content:
The rain came down in cold sheets, turning the cobblestones slick as pats of butter. I stood on the quayside, the Limmat flowing sluggish and grey beneath the trembling yellow streetlamps like a dead thing. It was just after midnight when I spotted it—not a log, not trash—but a dark shape snagged on the jutting stone where the current eddies. Called over the radio, we waded in through thigh-deep water that bit through the thin leather of my boots.

The woman lay there, half-submerged and half-exposed, her silk coat ballooned out with water, heavy as sin and clinging to her like a wet shroud. Her hair plastered to her face obscuring everything but the wide, unblinking stare. It wasn't the peaceful resignation of someone who gave up—it was the startled look of someone caught mid-breath, still expecting a ceiling to keep the river at bay. A smear of red lipstick gave her a final, tragic dignity above the bloating pallor of her skin.

She wore fitted gloves, soft leather still gripping her manicured fingers with all the pretension of life. And there was something else—the faint, sweet scent of French perfume cutting through the river's metallic bite for a heartbeat before it surrendered entirely. Someone had dressed her for death as if death were a social call.

The current didn't dare carry her far. Someone had placed her there deliberately, under the bleak stare of the Grossmünster's tower, treating the river as a trash chute but with weird, almost artful respect. This wasn't an accident. This was theater.

I stood there for a long moment, feeling the drizzle soak through my coat and the damp chill seep into my bones where decades of this work had already written cold into my marrow. Zurich doesn't casually dump bodies in the middle of the tourist district. The city's dark underbelly doesn't mistake the Limmat for oblivion unless they want the whole goddamned town to see it.

And as I watched the ripples spread outward from her still form, I knew this wasn't an ending. It was the opening line of a threat—or perhaps an invitation. Somewhere in this labyrinth of banking secrecy and smuggled goods, someone was probably very pleased with themselves right now.
